issues.title: Xray/REALITY: `dest` is always default and never follows the SNI set in the UI
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

For an Xray (VLESS + REALITY) container, the generated server config always contains

```json
"dest": "www.googletagmanager.com:443"
```

regardless of what the user configures. The **Server Name (SNI)** field on the Xray security settings page writes only to `serverNames`. There is no UI control for the masking site that `dest` is derived from, so `dest` permanently keeps its built-in default while `serverNames` follows the user's input.

The result is a `dest` and `serverNames` mismatch that the user cannot fix from the app and is never warned about.

**Why it's a problem**

REALITY relays the TLS handshake of every incoming connection to the configured target site, and an unauthenticated visitor is served that site (`dest` is the legacy name of that field, current Xray-core documents it as `target` and treats the two as aliases).

The [official REALITY documentation](https://xtls.github.io/en/config/transports/reality.html) states that `serverNames` has to be consistent with it:

> Usually this should stay consistent with `target`. In practice, valid values are any SNI accepted by the server according to the behavior of `target`, and typically refer to the SAN values on the returned certificate.

The config this app generates cannot satisfy that, because the two fields are driven by different inputs and only one of them is reachable from the UI.

With the mismatch in place, an active prober that connects to the server's IP with the configured SNI is forwarded to `www.googletagmanager.com`, which does not serve that name. It answers with an unrelated Google certificate or fails the handshake — exactly the anomaly REALITY exists to avoid. The whole point of choosing a masking site is defeated, and the user believes they have chosen one because the app offered them a field.

The mismatch does not break authorized clients, since the REALITY client authenticates via the REALITY signature rather than by validating the certificate chain against the SNI. That is why the problem is silent.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Add a self-hosted server, install the **Xray** container.
2. Open the protocol settings, set **Server Name (SNI)** to any domain other than the default, e.g. `example.com`.
3. Save.
4. On the server, read the generated config from inside the container:
   ```
   sudo docker exec amnezia-xray cat /opt/amnezia/xray/server.json
   ```
**Actual behavior**

```json
"realitySettings": {
    "dest": "www.googletagmanager.com:443",
    "fingerprint": "chrome",
    "privateKey": "...",
    "serverNames": ["example.com"],
    "shortIds": ["..."]
}
```

`dest` and `serverNames` refer to two unrelated sites.

**Expected behavior**

Either of:

- `dest` follows the configured name, so the generated config is self-consistent; or
- the masking site is exposed as its own UI field next to SNI, with validation that the entered SNI is served by the chosen `dest`.

At minimum the app should not silently produce a config whose `dest` and `serverNames` disagree.

**Notes from the code**

Not a diagnosis, just what turned up while looking for a workaround. Line references point at the `5.0.1.5` tag; the same code is present in current `dev`.

- `dest` is built from `XrayServerConfig::site`, `serverNames` from `XrayServerConfig::sni` - two independent fields ([`xrayConfigurator.cpp#L418-L425`](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/blob/5.0.1.5/client/core/configurators/xrayConfigurator.cpp#L418-L425)). Both are seeded with the same default at container creation ([`installerBase.cpp#L87`](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/blob/5.0.1.5/client/core/installers/installerBase.cpp#L87)).
- `SiteRole` exists in the model, but no QML page binds it and `grep -rn "site" client/ui/qml/Pages2/PageProtocolXray*.qml` returns nothing. The only exposed field is `Server Name (SNI)` → `SniRole` ([`PageProtocolXraySecuritySettings.qml#L275`](https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/blob/5.

issues.title: [Android] Per-app split tunneling bypass via unauthenticated local SOCKS5 listener on 127.0.0.1:10808
issues.body:
**Summary**

When AmneziaVPN is active on Android (X-ray profile), it exposes a SOCKS5 listener on 127.0.0.1:10808 that accepts unauthenticated connections. Because Android loopback is shared across apps, another application can connect to this listener. As a result, an app excluded from VPN routing via per-app split tunneling can still send traffic through the VPN by using the local SOCKS5 proxy. This behavior may unintentionally weaken the isolation guarantees of split tunneling and could increase the detectability of VPN usage in environments where app-level network monitoring is employed.


**Environment** 
- **App version**: 4.8.14.5
- **Android version**: 15
- **Device**: Samsung Galaxy S25
- **Protocol used**: Xray
- **Split tunneling**: Enabled (Termux excluded from VPN)

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Install AmneziaVPN and configure a working connection.
2. Enable **Per-app VPN** (split tunneling) and **exclude Termux** (or any test app with `INTERNET` permission).
3. Connect to the VPN.
4. In Termux, run:
   ```bash
   # Verify that direct traffic is not using the VPN
   curl -s https://ifconfig.me/ip
   # Expected: your real public IP
   
   # Check whether the localhost proxy is reachable
   nc -vz -w1 127.0.0.1 10808
   # Observed: connection succeeds only while VPN is active
   
   # Send traffic through the local SOCKS5 proxy from excluded app
   curl -s --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:10808 --connect-timeout 10 https://ifconfig.me/ip
   # Observed: VPN exit IP

**Observed behavior**
- Port `127.0.0.1:10808` is open **only when VPN is active**.
- The listener accepts SOCKS5 connections without authentication.
- An app excluded from VPN routing can still reach the VPN exit by using this localhost proxy.

**Expected Behavior**
Applications excluded from VPN routing should not be able to send traffic through the VPN tunnel via a localhost proxy, unless this behavior is explicitly documented and user-controlled. If a local listener is required for internal purposes, access should be restricted to the app's own components.

**Security Impact**
If the proxy accepts unauthenticated connections and forwards traffic through the VPN tunnel:
- User-configured per-app routing policies can be bypassed by any app with INTERNET permission.
- Traffic that the user explicitly intended to route directly may leak through the VPN (or vice versa).
- The presence of an open, unauthenticated localhost proxy may serve as a detectable signal of VPN usage to monitoring applications.

**Operational relevance**
In environments where applications or platforms monitor network behavior for signs of VPN usage, this issue may increase the detectability of VPN use. Because an app excluded from VPN routing can still access the VPN tunnel via localhost, it can both infer that the VPN is active and send probe traffic through the tunnel. This may also aid enumeration of VPN egress IPs and contribute to blocking of VPN endpoints. This consideration is particularly relevant given recent reports of app-level VPN detection guidelines being distributed to IT platforms [1][2].

**Suggested Mitigations**
- Require SOCKS5 authentication (username/password) for the localhost listener, if the feature is intended for external use.
- If the listener is only needed for internal IPC, consider using a private communication channel (e.g., Unix domain socket with restrictive permissions, or Android Binder with UID verification) instead of a shared TCP port on loopback.
- Document the behavior and its implications in the app's settings or security notes, so users can make informed decisions about split tunneling usage.


**References**
1. **Technical analysis of localhost proxy bypass in mobile VPN clients** (Russian):  
   https://habr.com/ru/articles/1020080/
   
2. **Community discussion: MinDigital guidelines for VPN detection** (Russian):  
   https://habr.com/ru/news/1019646/  
   *Summary: Russian Ministry of Digital Development issued guide

[iOS 4.8.21] OpenVPN over Cloak hangs because the local Cloak listener does not start
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

OpenVPN over Cloak hangs indefinitely on iOS in AmneziaVPN 4.8.21.0. The same server/profile works from AmneziaVPN on macOS, and AmneziaWG 2 works from the same iPhone.

This appears to be a regression of #2072.

**To reproduce**

1. Install/configure OpenVPN over Cloak through AmneziaVPN.
2. Import/create a fresh user profile on iPhone.
3. Tap Connect.
4. The app remains in the connecting state and no traffic reaches the Cloak server.

Deleting/recreating the profile and rebooting the iPhone do not change the behavior.

**Expected behavior**

The Cloak listener starts inside the packet-tunnel extension, then OpenVPN connects through the local listener and the tunnel becomes active.

**Sanitized diagnostic evidence**

- The iOS packet-tunnel extension starts successfully.
- The extension then repeatedly receives TCP `ECONNREFUSED` while connecting to its loopback OpenVPN endpoint (`127.0.0.1:1194`).
- No corresponding traffic reaches the server.
- This is consistent with the OpenVPN configuration being redirected to the local endpoint while the Cloak listener is not running.
- No credentials, server addresses, profile contents, or device identifiers are included here. A sanitized log excerpt can be provided if needed.

**Source/package evidence**

- Tag `4.8.21.0` still calls `configuration.setPTCloak()` in `client/platforms/ios/PacketTunnelProvider+OpenVPN.swift`.
- The same release line embeds the prebuilt `OpenVPNAdapter.framework` from the `client/3rd-prebuilt` submodule.
- At the submodule commit pinned by `4.8.21.0` (`4680bd8fb4173ad921f6181f7843ee5ae99b039b`), the iOS `OpenVPNAdapter` Mach-O is a dynamically linked shared library.
- #2645 (`fix(ios): link OpenVPNAdapter statically`) was merged into `dev` on 2026-05-30, but that fix is not present in the separate `4.8.21.0` release history.

The missing release-line equivalent of #2645 is therefore a likely cause, although I cannot produce an App Store-signed build locally to prove the complete fix.

**Smartphone**

- Device: iPhone 16
- OS: iOS 26.5.2
- AmneziaVPN: 4.8.21.0 (build 0)

**Additional context**

Could the team confirm whether the static-link fix (or its equivalent for the prebuilt release branch) will be backported, and whether there is an ETA for a TestFlight/App Store build?

If maintainers identify the intended target branch and artifact update path, I can prepare a focused PR rather than changing the wrong branch or submitting a binary-only workaround.

issues.title: [BUG] [macOS] 5.1.0.6: imported AWG profile loses a single DNS address
issues.body:
On macOS with AmneziaVPN 5.1.0.6, importing an AmneziaWG `.conf` containing one private DNS address leaves macOS using the application defaults, `1.1.1.1` and `1.0.0.1`. The tunnel and private HTTPS work, but private names do not resolve.

Re-importing the same profile with the private DNS address listed twice fixes resolution. No keys, routes or other settings were changed.

In `client/core/controllers/selfhosted/importController.cpp`, `ImportController::extractWireGuardConfig()` still requires two IPv4 DNS captures. A single address therefore leaves dns1/dns2 unset, and `NativeServerConfig::getDnsPair()` falls back to application DNS.

Expected: preserve a valid single DNS address without silently substituting public resolvers.

issues.title: [Feature Request] Support for URL-based  Subscriptions with Auto-Update  (v2rayN/Hiddify/Happ standard)
issues.body:
```markdown
### Summary

We propose adding native support for
**URL-based configuration subscriptions** to
the AmneziaVPN client, following the de-facto
ecosystem standard established by clients
like Happ, Incy, v2rayN/v2rayNG, Hiddify, and
Sing-box.

Currently, configurations in AmneziaVPN must
be imported individually (one `vpn://` key,
file, or QR code at a time). For
administrators managing multiple servers or
adjusting endpoints during ongoing ISP/DPI
blocks, this creates severe manual overhead.

---

### Background & Technical Context

In the current client architecture:
1. **Self-hosted configs are completely
static:** There is no mechanism for an
administrator to push updated endpoints (IPs,
ports, or AmneziaWG obfuscation parameters
like `Jc`/`Jmin`/`Jmax`/`H1`-`H4`) to
end-users without manually issuing new keys.
2. **Legacy API v1 was deprecated:** The
historical `api_endpoint` field in JSON
configs is now rejected with
`ErrorCode::LegacyApiV1NotSupportedError` in
`importController.cpp`.
3. **Amnezia Gateway v2/v3 is proprietary &
hardcoded:** The modern auto-updating
subsystem (`SubscriptionController` +
`libagw`) relies on hardcoded keys and
endpoints (`PROD_AGW_PUBLIC_KEY`,
`PROD_S3_ENDPOINT` in `CMakeLists.txt`) and
is restricted to `amnezia-premium`,
`amnezia-free`, and `external-premium`.
Self-hosted admins and third-party community
providers cannot use it.

Introducing a standard HTTP(S) subscription
mechanism solves this cleanly without
burdening Amnezia's own gateway
infrastructure.

---

### Proposed Solution & Specifications

#### 1. Import Mechanism
* **Input:** Allow importing via HTTPS URL
(pasting URL, scanning a subscription QR
code, or opening via Deeplink).
* **Deeplink:** Support 1-click import via
custom scheme, e.g.:

`amnezia://import-sub?url=https%3A%2F%2Fexamp
le.com%2Fsub`
* **Grouping:** Imported servers should
automatically be grouped under the
subscription name in the UI.

#### 2. Subscription Payload Format
* A standard HTTP(S) `GET` endpoint returning
a list of configurations (plain text or
standard Base64-encoded, newline-separated):
  * `vpn://...` connection strings.
  * Native AmneziaWG / AmneziaXRay (VLESS)
JSON blocks or WireGuard configs.

#### 3. Standard HTTP Headers Support
Adopt standard subscription metadata headers
widely supported across clients:
* **`profile-title`** (or
`Content-Disposition: filename=...`): Display
name of the subscription / server group.
* **`profile-update-interval`**: Recommended
auto-refresh interval in hours (e.g. `12` or
`24`).
* **`subscription-userinfo`**: Key-value
pairs for quota and validity:
  `upload=1073741824; download=5368709120;
total=107374182400; expire=1735689600`
  *(Used to render remaining data transfer
and subscription expiration date in the UI).*
* **`profile-web-page-url`**: URL to user
billing/dashboard.
* **`support-url`**: URL to support
channel/bot.

#### 4. Synchronization & Update Lifecycle
* **Update triggers:**
  * Automatically on application startup.
  * Periodically in the background via a
timer derived from `profile-update-interval`.
  * On-demand via a manual "Refresh
Subscription" button in the UI.
* **Diff reconciliation:**
  * Servers removed from the subscription URL
should be deleted or marked inactive.
  * Newly added servers are registered into
the subscription group.
  * Modified endpoints (changed IP, port, or
AWG parameters) are updated in-place without
breaking client-side custom settings (like
split tunneling rules).

#### 5. User Management & Controls
* Option to rename the subscription group.
* Toggle to enable/disable background
auto-updates.
* Option to delete the entire subscription
and all associated profiles in one click.

---

### Why This Matters

1. **Anti-Censorship Agility:** In
high-censorship environments (e.g., TSPU/RKN
in Russia, Iran, China), server IPs and ports
are blocked rapidly. Administrators can
change endpoints on the backend, and all
clients update seamlessly without user
inter

issues.title: Windows XRay selects disconnected adapter with stale default gateway
issues.body:
Environment:
- AmneziaVPN 5.0.1.5
- Windows 11 build 26200
- XRay core 26.7.28
- Active Ethernet connection
- Disconnected Wi-Fi adapter retaining an IPv4 address and default route

Problem:
XRay appears connected, but DNS resolution and web browsing fail. An Android client using the same server works correctly.

Observed diagnostics:
- The tun2 adapter is created successfully at 10.33.0.2.
- DNS servers 1.1.1.1 and 1.0.0.1 are assigned to tun2.
- TCP/443 connections through tun2 succeed.
- UDP/53 requests through tun2 time out.
- TCP/53 requests through tun2 fail or are closed.
- tun2 reports traffic with no adapter packet errors or discarded packets.
- Authenticated requests directly through Amnezia's embedded SOCKS/XRay endpoint fail after successful SOCKS authentication.
- A server-side packet capture receives the Windows XRay connection but sees no corresponding outbound DNS or web traffic.
- Server-side TCP and UDP DNS tests through the same VLESS/Reality configuration succeed.
- The Windows and server XRay core versions are both 26.7.28.

Root-cause indication:
NetworkUtilities::getGatewayAndIface() enumerates adapters returned by GetAdaptersAddresses() and retains the last adapter containing an IPv4 gateway. It does not check OperStatus and does not select the best route.

Xray::startXray() then uses that interface index with IP_UNICAST_IF for every outbound XRay socket.

The disconnected Wi-Fi adapter still had an IPv4 address and an active default route. Disabling Wi-Fi at the adapter level removed that route and immediately made XRay work.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Connect Windows to the internet through Ethernet.
2. Leave a Wi-Fi adapter disconnected but retaining an IPv4 address and default route.
3. Connect an XRay Reality profile in AmneziaVPN.
4. Observe that Amnezia reports a connection, but DNS and web browsing fail.
5. Disable the Wi-Fi adapter with Disable-NetAdapter.
6. Reconnect AmneziaVPN.
7. Observe that DNS and web browsing now work.

Expected behavior:
Amnezia should select the active adapter used by the best route to the VPN server.

Suggested fix:
Use GetBestRoute/GetBestRoute2 for the VPN server address, or ignore adapters whose OperStatus is not IfOperStatusUp. Do not select the last adapter returned by GetAdaptersAddresses().

Workaround:
Disable disconnected adapters that retain default gateways.

issues.title: AWG self-hosted: H1–H4 hardcoded to 1/2/3/4 (WireGuard defaults), and ranged H breaks the client in 3.1 mode
issues.body:
When installing AmneziaWG on a self-hosted server via the app, H1–H4 are always set to 1/2/3/4 — see `client/core/utils/constants/protocolConstants.h` (`defaultInitPacketMagicHeader[] = "1"` etc.) used by `client/core/installers/awgInstaller.cpp`, and again in `importController.cpp`. These are the standard WireGuard message-type values, so header obfuscation is effectively disabled: a DPI sees plain WireGuard packet types at offset 0.

Per the amneziawg-go docs, H1–H4 also accept ranges (`x-y`), which is the AWG 2.0+ way to randomize headers per packet. But if the server uses ranged H together with AWG 3.1 parameters (`HeaderProtectionKey`, `RandomTrailers`, etc.), the client connects yet throughput collapses to <1 Mbit/s and the log is flooded with `Received packet with invalid mac1` (hundreds per second). Ranged H with plain AWG 2.0 (no 3.1 keys) works fine in the same client.

Tests I ran on the same server:

- ranged H + 3.1 keys → <1 Mbit/s, invalid mac1 flood
- fixed H = 1/2/3/4 + 3.1 keys → full speed (180 Mbit/s)
- fixed random H (e.g. H1 = 1383913556, H2 = 974520887, H3 = 1095760722, H4 = 264520681) + 3.1 keys → full speed as well

Questions:
1. Why are 1/2/3/4 hardcoded instead of generating random values or ranges (as the 2.0 spec intends)? A single hardcoded set also means all self-hosted deployments share one signature.
2. Is ranged H officially supported by the client in 3.1 mode? If not, could the app warn on such configs instead of silently degrading to <1 Mbit/s?

Related: #2942 (3.0 parameters silently dropped on import).

Environment: AmneziaVPN desktop (Windows), server `amneziavpn/amneziawg-go:latest` in userspace mode (no kernel module on host).

issues.title: AmneziaWG v2: server generates config with I1 commented out while client keeps I1 active — handshake never completes
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
After installing an AmneziaWG (v2) server, the connection never completes the handshake. The client's AmneziaWG settings have the **I1 ("Special junk 1")** field populated with a value, but the server's generated config (`/opt/amnezia/awg/awg0.conf`) has the same I1 value **commented out**. Since the client sends packets using I1 obfuscation but the server doesn't expect/apply it, packets are silently dropped and the handshake never completes — no error is shown, the app just stays stuck on "Connecting...".

**To Reproduce**
1. Add a new server in AmneziaVPN client (Windows) via SSH, using a fresh Ubuntu 22.04 VPS.
2. Let the client install AmneziaWG (v2) automatically.
3. Try to connect — the app stays on "Connecting..." indefinitely.
4. On the server, run `docker exec -it amnezia-awg2 wg show` — no "latest handshake" ever appears for the peer.
5. On the server, run `docker exec -it amnezia-awg2 cat /opt/amnezia/awg/awg0.conf` and compare the `I1` line against the client's AmneziaWG settings screen (Settings → AmneziaWG → I1 – Special junk 1). The values match, but on the server it's commented out (`# I1 = ...`) while the client actively sends it.
6. This was reproduced on 5 separate clean installs in a row (server rebuilt from scratch each time).

**Expected behavior**
The I1–I5 junk packet settings generated for the client should match what's actually enabled in the server's config. Either both should have I1 enabled, or the installer shouldn't disable it server-side after generating it client-side. The connection should establish a handshake successfully on first install without manual config editing.

**Log files**
`tcpdump -ni any udp port <port>` on the server during a connection attempt shows client packets arriving every ~5 seconds (WireGuard retry behavior) and being forwarded into the container's `awg0`/veth interfaces, but no reply packets are ever sent back.

Server config (`awg0.conf`), relevant lines (keys redacted):
```
PrivateKey = <REDACTED>
Address = 10.8.1.0/24
ListenPort = <SERVER_PORT>
Jc = 4
Jmin = 10
Jmax = 50
S1 = 98
S2 = 52
S3 = 33
S4 = 15
H1 = 664080018-1212358601
H2 = 1757041261-1858300431
H3 = 2044350858-2117832879
H4 = 2129609579-2138086604
# I1 = <r 2><b 0x858000010001000000000669636c6f756403636f6d0000010001c00c000100010000105a00044d583737>
# I2 =
# I3 =
# I4 =
# I5 =
[Peer]
PublicKey = <REDACTED>
PresharedKey = <REDACTED>
AllowedIPs = 10.8.1.1/32
```

Client's I1 field (Settings → AmneziaWG) has the same value **active** (not commented), while I2–I5 are empty on both sides.

**Screenshots**
(attached separately — client's AmneziaWG settings page showing I1 populated)

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
- OS: Windows
- Version: 4.8.19.0 (Jun 15 2026, 129ae44ed)

**Server (please complete the following information):**
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
- Deployment: Docker-based install via AmneziaVPN client, `amnezia-awg2` container, AmneziaWG v2 protocol

**Additional context**
Manually clearing the I1 field in the client's AmneziaWG settings (so both client and server have I1 disabled) immediately fixed the connection — the handshake completed right after and `wg show` showed a valid "latest handshake". This looks like a reproducible bug in how the installer generates/syncs the I1–I5 obfuscation parameters between the client and server configs, not a one-off network issue — happened consistently across 5 clean reinstalls with different fresh VPS instances.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
When connecting to AmneziaVPN (version 4.8.12.9 and newer) on my Arch Linux system (Omarchy 3.8.2), internet connectivity is completely lost after a successful VPN connection. DNS resolution to the configured DNS server still works, but general internet access is broken.
The issue does not occur in version 4.8.11.4, which works correctly. If I’m not mistaken, some versions newer than 4.8.11.4 used to work fine previously, so it seems like something may have broken either on the client side or due to some recent system update on my side.

---

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Install AmneziaVPN 4.8.12.9 or newer from AUR
2. Launch the AmneziaVPN client
3. Connect to VPN configuration (vless in my case)
4. Internet connectivity is lost immediately after connection

---

**Expected behavior**

Internet access should continue working normally through the VPN connection, as it does in version 4.8.11.4.

---

**Log files**
Logs collected immediately after reproducing the issue. I connected to the VPN, then attempted to access the internet via both a web browser and terminal (ping to google.com), but both failed due to complete loss of connectivity. After that, I disconnected from the VPN.

[vpn-debug.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28840429/vpn-debug.tar.gz)

---

**Desktop:**

* OS: Arch Linux (Omarchy 3.8.2, rolling release)
* Kernel: 7.0.11-arch1-1

---

**Additional context**

* Rolling back to AmneziaVPN 4.8.11.4 restores full functionality.
* DNS server configured via VPN remains reachable in affected versions.
* Issue occurs consistently across all tested VPN configurations.
* Root cause is unknown; initial troubleshooting did not identify the issue.

issues.title: macOS Tahoe 26.5 — AmneziaWG stuck on `status`, never `connected`; iOS works on same Wi‑Fi
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

On macOS Tahoe (26.3.1–26.5), AmneziaVPN 4.8.15.4 cannot complete an AmneziaWG (`amnezia-awg2`) connection to a self-hosted VPS. The app stays on “Connecting…” (or disconnects after a few seconds). Application logs never show `Parse command: connected` or `Handshake completed`.

The same server and config work on **iPhone on the same Wi‑Fi**. On Mac, `wg show` on the server often shows **no `latest handshake`**, and `tcpdump` on UDP port 585 sometimes captures **0 packets** while the client appears to be connecting.

Additional symptoms:

- Routes `0.0.0.0/1` and `128.0.0.0/1` are installed via `utun4`, but traffic does not work (`curl` / DNS timeouts).
- An active **SSH session to the server IP freezes** when VPN connect starts (server IP is routed into the dead tunnel unless a manual host route is added).
- **Site-based split tunneling** (`VpnAllExceptSites`, route mode 2) does not fix the issue; logs still never show `connected`.
- Internal route mode is often logged as `Settings::VpnOnlyForwardSites` while site split is disabled (`route mode 0`), which looks inconsistent.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Install AmneziaVPN **4.8.15.4** on **macOS Tahoe 26.5** (x86_64).
2. Add a self-hosted server with **AmneziaWG** (container `amnezia-awg2`, UDP port **585**).
3. Confirm the same connection works on **iOS** (same Wi‑Fi, same server/config).
4. On Mac, click **Connect** once and wait 30–60 seconds.
5. Observe: UI shows **Connecting…** (or disconnects); no stable VPN.
6. (Optional) While connecting, run on server: `docker exec amnezia-awg2 wg show` and `tcpdump -ni eth0 udp port 585` → often no handshake / no UDP packets.
7. (Optional) With SSH open to the server, click **Connect** → SSH session stops responding until VPN is disabled.

## Expected behavior

- After `Daemon connected` → `Parse command: status`, the client should proceed to `Parse command: connected` and `Handshake completed`.
- VPN should reach **Connected** state; `curl https://ifconfig.me` should show the VPS public IP.
- Server `wg show` should show `latest handshake` and increasing `transfer`.
- Split tunnel exclusions (e.g. server IP) should work on macOS, or at least not leave the client stuck on `status`.

## Log files

Attach the full application log file. Typical pattern on every attempt:

```
Trying to connect to VPN ... container is amnezia-awg2, route mode is Settings::VpnOnlyForwardSites
Site split tunneling is disabled, route mode is 0
LocalSocketController : Daemon connected
LocalSocketController : Parse command: status
... (no "connected", no "Handshake completed") ...
LocalSocketController : Deactivating
Parse command: disconnected
VpnProtocol::setConnectionState "Отключено"
```

When split tunnel was enabled:

```
route mode is Settings::VpnAllExceptSites
Site split tunneling is enabled, route mode is 2
```

Same result: only `status`, then disconnect — never `connected`.

Also seen:

```
Reconnect triggered on Connecting during inappropriate state ... ignoring
```

(Full log session: 2026-05-21, macOS Tahoe 26.3.1 → 26.5, AmneziaVPN 4.8.15.4.)

- Amnezia UI stuck on “Connecting…”

- `ifconfig utun4` / `netstat -rn` showing `0/1` and `128.0/1` via `utun4` while not fully connected

issues.title: Linux XRay regression after 4.8.11.4: 4.8.12+ no longer ships xray binary
issues.body:
Hi maintainers. I’m trying to understand whether this is an expected backend/packaging change or a Linux regression. I can provide more logs if helpful.

### Short version

XRay/VLESS works for me with AmneziaVPN `4.8.10.0` on Linux, but does not work with newer Linux releases such as `4.8.14.5` and `4.8.15.4`.

The same self-hosted VLESS server/inbound works from another machine, and also works on this laptop after downgrading to `4.8.10.0`.

### Package difference I found

I inspected the Linux release installer payloads and found this boundary:

| Version | Linux payload contains `client/bin/xray`? |
|---|---|
| `4.8.10.0` | yes, `client/bin/xray` + `xray.sha256` |
| `4.8.11.4` | yes, `client/bin/xray` + `xray.sha256` |
| `4.8.12.7` | no |
| `4.8.12.8` | no |
| `4.8.12.9` | no |
| `4.8.14.1` | no |
| `4.8.14.5` | no |
| `4.8.15.0` | no |
| `4.8.15.4` | no |

This seems to match a source-level change:

- `4.8.11.4`: `client/protocols/xrayprotocol.cpp` launches an external `xray` executable.
- `4.8.12.x+`: XRay is started through IPC and handled by `AmneziaVPN-service` via `amnezia_xray_start()`.
- The likely transition is #1899 (`feat: native split-tunneling for xray`).

So maybe removing the standalone `xray` binary was intentional. The problem is that the replacement path does not appear to work on my Linux system.

### Runtime symptom on broken versions

On `4.8.14.5` / `4.8.15.4`:

- UI says connected.
- `tun2` is created.
- `tun2socks` runs and points at a local SOCKS listener owned by `AmneziaVPN-service`.
- There is no separate `xray` process.
- The local SOCKS listener accepts the connection.
- `curl` through that SOCKS proxy sends the TLS ClientHello, then waits until timeout.
- `tcpdump` on the uplink interface sees no packets to the VLESS server during that SOCKS test.

So this does not look like only DNS: even a direct SOCKS test without DNS does not complete.

### Environment

- Ubuntu 26.04 LTS
- Kernel `7.0.0-15-generic`
- KDE, X11
- Protocol: self-hosted XRay/VLESS
- Working client version: `4.8.10.0`
- Broken client versions tested: `4.8.14.5`, `4.8.15.4`

### Questions

1. Was the standalone Linux `xray` binary intentionally removed starting with `4.8.12.x`?
2. Is the embedded `AmneziaVPN-service` XRay backend expected to fully replace it on Linux?
3. If yes, what logs or debug checks would help identify why the embedded backend accepts the local SOCKS stream but appears not to send traffic to the VLESS server?

Thanks.

issues.title: Internet stops working after connecting to AmneziaVPN on Arch Linux (NetworkManager conflict)
issues.body:
When I connect to AmneziaVPN on Arch Linux (with NetworkManager), my internet stops working. The issue is resolved only after manually running these commands:
sudo ip route flush dev amn0
sudo ip route add default dev amn0
echo "nameserver 1.1.1.1" | sudo tee /etc/resolv.conf
sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved

Expected behavior:
Internet should work normally after connecting to VPN, without manual route/DNS fixes.

Steps to reproduce:
    1.Install AmneziaVPN on Arch Linux (with NetworkManager).
    2.Connect to any VPN server.
    3.Observe loss of internet connectivity.

Possible causes:
    AmneziaVPN does not properly update routes for amn0.
    Conflict with NetworkManager (tries to manage routes/DNS, but AmneziaVPN overrides them).
    DNS leak or incorrect /etc/resolv.conf handling with systemd-resolved.

Temporary workaround:
Manually setting default route and DNS (as shown above).

System info:
    OS: Arch Linux
    NetworkManager: Installed and enabled
    AmneziaVPN

issues.title: openglrenderer unable to match the desired swap behavior
issues.body:
**Опишите баг**
При попытке захостить vpn сервер появляется ошибка "openglrenderer unable to match the desired swap behavior".

**Чтобы воспроизвести**
Шаги для воспроизведения ошибки:
1. При первом запуске приложения выбрать пункт "self-hosted".
2. На сервере установить docker.
3. Убрать необходимость подтверждать паролем root действия на сервере.
4. Ввести данные сервера в приложении.
5. Выбрать режим автоматической установки.
6. Получить ошибку 202(Server error: Docker container missing).

issues.title: Feature Request: Add CLI support for AmneziaVPN client
issues.body:
# Request
Hello! I would like to request a feature to work on later — **amneziacli**.

## Functionality

The following command line interface should implement at least three methods:
1. `select(Server servername)` — Chooses a server from the Servers list.
2. `connect()` — Connects to the specified server
3. `disconnect()` — Disconnects from the specified server

## Why

On my laptop I often encounter a problem with networking, where I need to:
1. Disable VPN
2. Reconnect to my network
3. Enable VPN back

All of this can only be done manually via GUI of the Amnezia client. This approach is very inconvenient and awkward.

Also, the CLI solution can be a better UX for some users. 

---

**Thank you for your time.**

issues.body:
Version Amnezia VPN 4.8.7.2
When your application is running, the video card starts to malfunction. My graphics card: KFA2 GeForce RTX 4060 X Black [46NSL8MD8MEK].
The essence is as follows. Normally, the video card works as follows "screenshot 1": Under medium loads, the maximum frequency of video cores is 2865 MHz, and their use is only 40%.
When your AmneziaVPN application is running, the situation is as follows: with an average load, the number of video cores is almost 80%+ maximum, but the frequency is average, only around 1100 MHz, "screenshot 2".
At the same time, the performance of the video card remains the same, and under high loads, all cores also operate at maximum frequency.
The essence of abnormal behavior is: That the number of cores involved increases first, and only then their frequency. Normally, it should be the other way around.
At the same time, if you use the AmneziaWG application with the same configuration files for VPN, then this behavior of the video card disappears and it always works normally.

If the window is moved from side to side, the situation normalizes/unnormalizes again, depending on the initial state of the state. issues.title: Regex on split tunelling
issues.body:
---

**Describe the bug**
Split tunneling functionality appears to only accept explicit IP addresses or hostnames, and does not support the use of wildcard characters (e.g., `*`) for broader domain matching within application exclusion rules. This prevents users from easily specifying entire services or subdomains for split tunneling.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Go to the split tunneling configuration section of the application.
2. Attempt to add a rule to exclude a domain using a wildcard, for example, `*.discord.gg` or `*.discord.com`.
3. Observe that the input field either rejects the wildcard syntax or the rule does not function as expected, meaning traffic to subdomains of discord.gg or discord.com still routes through the VPN.

**Expected behavior**
The split tunneling feature should allow the use of wildcard characters (e.g., `*`) in domain specifications, effectively acting as a form of regex, to enable easier and more comprehensive exclusion of applications or services (e.g., `*.discord.gg`, `*.discord.com`). When such a rule is applied, all traffic matching the wildcard pattern should be routed outside the VPN.

**Log files**
[Please attach relevant log files here if available, demonstrating the attempt to add a wildcard rule and any resulting errors or unexpected routing behavior.]

**Screenshots**
[If applicable, add screenshots showing the input field rejecting the wildcard or the rule being entered but not functioning correctly.]

**Additional context**
The current limitation to only explicit IP addresses or hostnames makes managing split tunneling rules cumbersome, especially for applications or services that utilize multiple subdomains. Allowing wildcard matching would significantly improve usability and flexibility.

issues.title: linux DNS error while using amnezia
issues.body:
I've been using the app with the amneziaWG protocol on my linux for a couple of months without any issues. However, after updating to version 4.8.2.3, my VPN via WireGuard stopped working, displaying a DNS error. Through testing, I realized the issue seems to be related to the killswitch, though I haven't pinpointed the exact fix.

I attempted manual reinstallation and even reverted to older versions, but the problem persisted on this specific computer. As a temporary workaround, I switched to xray.

Today, after updating to version 4.8.3.1, I encountered a new issue: all available protocols fail when the killswitch is enabled. What should i do to resolve this?

issues.title: Importing dependencies on the Android version of the app does not work.
issues.body:
# Importing dependencies on the Android version of the app does not work

When trying to import a file with pre-prepared configurations, Amnezia does not issue an error, but simply exits the program. Accordingly, the configurations are not saved and the application becomes inoperable. 

## The standard features of the application also raise some questions

The basic functionality of the application does not work as a VPN service, but as some kind of host bridge, which is why access to the services is not carried out, but the connection speed drops.

##  An implicit read file when trying to import dependencies.

There is no clear file extension when importing boot data prepared by other people. Make a restriction on typing.

issues.title: UDP connection does not work with split tunneling
Ipc::Init failed or Error code 101 on OpenRC Linux systems(Gentoo, Suse, etc..)
issues.body:
**What happens**
When trying to connect to the server, error 101 occurs, if you run AmneziaVPN from the terminal, you can see Ipc::init failed.

***How to solve***
The error occurs when the AmneziaVPN server is not started in the system. It happens because OpenRC support has not been added yet. To solve this you need to manually create the service.

Here is the code for the OpenRC to start AmneziaVPN service:
```
#!/sbin/openrc-run

description="AmneziaVPN Service"

pidfile="/run/amnezia-vpn.pid"

depend() {
    after net
}

start() {
    ebegin "Starting AmneziaVPN Service"
    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/AmneziaVPN/client/lib
    start-stop-daemon --start --background --make-pidfile --pidfile "$pidfile" --exec /opt/AmneziaVPN/service/AmneziaVPN-service.sh
    eend $?
}

stop() {
    ebegin "Stopping AmneziaVPN Service"
    start-stop-daemon --stop --pidfile "$pidfile"
    eend $?
}
```

Steps:
- Ensure that AmneziaVPN installed int /opt/AmneziaVPN, if is no
replace /opt/AmneziaVPN to yours AmneziaVPN installations root.
-Create the file /etc/init.d/AmneziaVPNd and put the code above to this file
-chmod +x /opt/AmneziaVPN/service/AmneziaVPN-service.sh
-Try to start the service manually:
```
rc-service AmneziaVPNd start
```
If problem is solved add this service on the startup of your system:
```
rc-update add AmneziaVPNd
```

***Conclusion***
I'd really appreciate to dev team if they will add support for OpenRC in the future.

issues.title: Xray protocol: changing SNI via UI updates `serverNames` but leaves `dest` unchanged, breaking REALITY handshake for strict clients (e.g. sing-box)
issues.body:
### Summary

When changing the SNI field ("Server name (sni)") for the **Xray** protocol via the Amnezia-client UI, the server-side `server.json` inside the `amnezia-xray` container is updated only in `realitySettings.serverNames`. The `realitySettings.dest` field is **not** updated and keeps the original default value (e.g. `www.googletagmanager.com:443`).

As a result, the server continues to fetch and present the TLS certificate of the old `dest` host, while advertising a different SNI to clients. This creates a mismatch between the requested SNI and the returned certificate.

### Affected setup

- Protocol: **Xray (VLESS + REALITY, xtls-rprx-vision)**
- Server: Amnezia self-hosted VPS, protocol installed via Amnezia-client (Docker container `amnezia-xray`)
- Container entrypoint: `dumb-init /opt/amnezia/start.sh`
- Config path inside container: `/opt/amnezia/xray/server.json`
- Clients used for testing: **sing-box 1.14.x** (TUN mode, strict certificate verification), plus Amnezia mobile clients (Android)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Xray protocol on a clean VPS via the Amnezia client (Docker container `amnezia-xray`).
2. In the Amnezia client UI, open the Xray protocol settings and change the **"Server name (SNI)"** field from the default value (e.g. `www.googletagmanager.com`) to another domain, for example `files.pythonhosted.org`.
3. Apply changes.
4. On the server, inspect the container config:
   ```bash
   docker exec -it amnezia-xray cat /opt/amnezia/xray/server.json
   ```

### Actual behavior

The config contains a **mismatch**:

```json
"realitySettings": {
    "dest": "www.googletagmanager.com:443",
    "fingerprint": "chrome",
    "privateKey": "...",
    "serverNames": [
        "files.pythonhosted.org"
    ],
    "shortIds": [
        "..."
    ]
}
```

- `serverNames` — updated to the new SNI entered in the UI.
- `dest` — **left unchanged** at the old default (`www.googletagmanager.com:443`).

Because REALITY uses `dest` as the source of the certificate it presents during the handshake, the server returns a certificate valid for `*.google-analytics.com` / `*.googletagmanager.com` while the client expects `files.pythonhosted.org`.

### Expected behavior

Changing the SNI in the UI should update **both** `serverNames` **and** `dest` (or at least provide a separate field / automatic synchronization), so that the presented certificate matches the advertised SNI.

### Impact

- **sing-box** (and any client that strictly verifies the certificate) fails to connect with:
  ```
  x509: certificate is valid for *.google-analytics.com, ..., not files.pythonhosted.org
  ```
- Amnezia mobile clients appear to work because they do not strictly verify the returned certificate, which **masks the bug** during normal use.
- The mismatched SNI/certificate pair is an anomaly in TLS traffic that can be flagged by DPI systems, potentially putting the server IP at risk of being blocked.

### Workaround

Manually editing `dest` inside the container fixes the issue:

```bash
docker cp amnezia-xray:/opt/amnezia/xray/server.json /root/server.json
# edit "dest" to match "serverNames", e.g. "files.pythonhosted.org:443"
python3 -m json.tool /root/server.json > /dev/null && echo "JSON OK"
docker cp /root/server.json amnezia-xray:/opt/amnezia/xray/server.json
docker restart amnezia-xray
```

However, this is fragile: any subsequent change to the Xray protocol via the Amnezia client UI (adding a client, changing SNI, etc.) overwrites `server.json` and reverts `dest` back to the old default, requiring the manual fix again.

### Suggested fix

In the Amnezia-client code that generates `server.json` for the Xray protocol, when the user changes the SNI, update `realitySettings.dest` accordingly (e.g. set `dest` to `<new_sni>:443`), or add an explicit `dest`/`target` field in the UI so both values can be configured and kept in sync.

### Environment

- Amnezia-client version: _5.0.3.0_
- Desktop OS: Windows 11
- Server OS: Debian 13
- Con

issues.title: Десктопный клиент использует устаревший дефолт MTU=1376 для AmneziaWG вместо MTU из импортированного профиля — вызывает «чёрную дыру» PMTU на AWG 3.x
issues.body:
Суть проблемы
На десктопных платформах (подтверждено на Windows; судя по коду, вероятно и на Linux, и на обычной сборке macOS без network-extension) клиент AmneziaWG откатывается на захардкоженный defaultMtu = "1376" в client/core/utils/constants/protocolConstants.h, вместо того чтобы использовать значение mtu из импортированного vpn://-профиля подключения. На мобильных сборках (Android/iOS/macOS network-extension) уже стоит defaultMtu = "1280".

// client/core/utils/constants/protocolConstants.h
namespace awg
{
    constexpr char defaultPort[] = "55424";
#if defined(Q_OS_ANDROID) || defined(Q_OS_IOS) || defined(MACOS_NE)
    constexpr char defaultMtu[] = "1280";
#else
    constexpr char defaultMtu[] = "1376";
#endif
Почему это важно
AmneziaWG 3.x добавляет обфускацию на каждый пакет сверх обычного WireGuard (HeaderProtectionKey, junk-пакеты, паддинг S1-S4). С учётом этого оверхеда, MTU в 1376 на туннельном интерфейсе оказывается достаточно большим, чтобы часть исходящих пакетов — заметнее всего крупные одиночные ответы вроде TLS ServerHello/Certificate или тела HTTP-ответа с картинкой — незаметно терялись где-то по пути (классическая «чёрная дыра» PMTU: ICMP "fragmentation needed" не доходит обратно до отправителя, поэтому пропавшие TCP-сегменты никогда не перепосылаются, и соединение просто виснет до таймаута).

Баг воспроизводится стабильно и легко демонстрируется: страница/домен, чей ответ в один всплеск занимает больше одного MTU-сегмента (часть сертификатов, тела картинок и т.д.), просто уходит в таймаут, а мелкие ответы (многие обычные сайты, короткие ответы вроде Google/Яндекс, адаптивно нарезанное видео) работают нормально. Мобильные клиенты этой проблемы не имеют, потому что у них дефолт уже 1280.

Подтверждённая первопричина
Проверено end-to-end на реальном сервере и реальном Windows-клиенте:

На сервере интерфейс AmneziaWG выставлен на MTU = 1280 (в серверном wg0.conf/awg0.conf).
Сгенерирован свежий vpn://-ключ для этого сервера, декодирован — подтверждено, что внутри embedded last_config JSON лежит "mtu": "1280".
Этот же ключ импортирован в Windows-клиент AmneziaVPN (также пробовали полностью удалить сервер из приложения и импортировать заново — результат тот же).
Get-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias "AmneziaVPN" -AddressFamily IPv4 на получившемся адаптере показывает NlMtu = 1376, а не 1280.
Захват пакетов на сервере (tcpdump на расшифрованном интерфейсе wg0) во время реального неудачного соединения показывает TCP SYN клиента с mss 1336 — это ровно то MSS, которое подразумевает MTU 1376 (1376 − 20 IP − 20 TCP = 1336), что подтверждает: реальный, живой туннельный интерфейс работает на 1376, а не на импортированных 1280.
Принудительная установка MTU командой netsh interface ipv4 set subinterface "AmneziaVPN" mtu=1280 store=persistent сразу же чинит ранее неработавшие сайты/картинки; при следующем переподключении VPN значение снова сбрасывается на 1376 (подтверждает, что клиент заново применяет свой дефолт при каждом коннекте).
Исправление
config.mtu в AwgProtocolConfig/WireGuardProtocolConfig подставляется из protocols::awg::defaultMtu / protocols::wireguard::defaultMtu только когда пустой (applyDefaultsToClientConfig, awgConfigModel.cpp:224-229 и аналогичный код в wireguardConfigModel.cpp) — то есть на недесктопных платформах он откатывается на устаревшую константу 1376 вместо того, чтобы донести реально импортированное значение. Минимальное и безопасное исправление — просто убрать разделение по платформам и везде использовать 1280, что уже совпадает с тем, что client/daemon/daemon.cpp:262-263 и так считает безопасным минимумом (if (config.m_deviceMTU < 1280) config.m_deviceMTU = 1280;):

-#if defined(Q_OS_ANDROID) || defined(Q_OS_IOS) || defined(MACOS_NE)
 constexpr char defaultMtu[] = "1280";
-#else
-constexpr char defaultMtu[] = "1376";
-#endif
(применяется к неймспейсам wireguard и awg в client/core/utils/constants/protocolConstants.h)

Патч приложен (amnezia-mtu-fix.patch).

Это исправление трогает только дефол

issues.title: [Windows][Regression] AmneziaWG 2.0 fails to connect on 5.0.1.5: wsasendmsg/wsarecvmsg invalid pointer error
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

После обновления клиента AmneziaVPN на Windows с **4.8.21.0** до **5.0.1.5** ни одно из ранее рабочих подключений (self-hosted AmneziaWG, сервер на протоколе **AmneziaWG 2.0**) больше не устанавливается: приложение зависает в статусе «Подключение…» и само разрывает соединение примерно через 28 секунд. Откат на 4.8.21.0 на том же ПК с тем же конфигом сразу восстанавливает работу.

## To Reproduce

1. Настроить AmneziaWG-подключение к self-hosted серверу, работающему на AmneziaWG 2.0 (в конфиге заданы `H1`–`H4` и `HeaderProtectionKey`)
2. Обновить клиент до 5.0.1.5
3. Нажать «Подключиться»

## Expected behavior

Handshake завершается за 1–2 секунды, как в 4.8.21.0.

## Desktop

- OS: Windows 11, Version 25H2 (x86_64)
- Клиент (не работает): AmneziaVPN 5.0.1.5, сборка `7d4f3e0f5`
- Клиент (работает): AmneziaVPN 4.8.21.0, сборка `72ee32af1`
- tunnel.dll: `WireGuard/0.3.15`, `Wintun/0.14` — одинаковы в обеих версиях
- Протокол: AmneziaWG, сервер self-hosted на AmneziaWG 2.0

## Log files

Прикладываю оба лог-файла целиком (клиентский `AmneziaVPN.log` и сервисный `AmneziaVPN-service.log`) для рабочего (v4.8.21.0) и нерабочего (v5.0.1.5) подключений — по ним видна полная последовательность.

Ключевой фрагмент service-лога 5.0.1.5, сразу после поднятия интерфейса:

```
[TUN] [AmneziaVPN] Failed to receive v4 packet: read udp4 0.0.0.0:51618: wsarecvmsg: The system detected an invalid pointer address in attempting to use a pointer argument in a call.
[TUN] [AmneziaVPN] Routine: receive incoming v4 - stopped
[TUN] [AmneziaVPN] Failed to receive v6 packet: read udp6 [::]:51618: wsarecvmsg: The system detected an invalid pointer address in attempting to use a pointer argument in a call.
[TUN] [AmneziaVPN] Routine: receive incoming v6 - stopped
```

Оба recv-воркера (v4 и v6) падают сразу после старта. Далее каждая попытка отправить handshake initiation проваливается той же ошибкой (повторяется каждые ~5 сек: retry 2, 3, 4, 5…):

```
[TUN] [AmneziaVPN] peer(Oc56…D1gg) - Failed to send handshake initiation: write udp4 0.0.0.0:51618-><VPN_SERVER_IP>:443: wsasendmsg: The system detected an invalid pointer address in attempting to use a pointer argument in a call.
```

В логе 4.8.21.0 recv v4/v6-воркеры стартуют и остаются активными без единой ошибки, handshake завершается за ~150 мс.

## Additional context

Сравнил оба service-лога построчно. Строка `Registered I/O is unavailable: ...invalid pointer address...` присутствует в обеих версиях идентично и, судя по всему, не является проблемой сама по себе — это ожидаемый триггер fallback'а на обычные (не-RIO) сокеты. Единственное **структурное** отличие в последовательности поднятия интерфейса — 4 новых вызова UAPI в 5.0.1.5, которых нет в 4.8.21.0:

```
UAPI: Updating h1 padding
UAPI: Updating h2 padding
UAPI: Updating h3 padding
UAPI: Updating h4 padding
...
UAPI: Updating header protection key
```

Это параметры Header Protection из AmneziaWG 2.0 (ranged-заголовки H1–H4 + ChaCha20 HeaderProtectionKey). Все остальные шаги (воркеры, правила firewall, маршруты, тот самый RIO-фолбэк) идентичны в обеих версиях и после фолбэка ни разу не ошибаются в 4.8.21.0.

Судя по блог-посту о 5.0.1.5, клиент перешёл на движок AmneziaWG 3.1, а self-hosted-серверы на AmneziaWG 2.0 (как в моём случае) поддерживаются как legacy через загруженный конфиг. Похоже, что именно код, который в Windows-реализации tunnel.dll собирает буфер/указатель для `WSARecvMsg`/`WSASendMsg` при активных `H1`–`H4`/`HeaderProtectionKey`, формирует некорректный указатель — из-за этого рвётся и приём, и отправка UDP одновременно, и handshake физически не может уйти на сервер. В 4.8.21.0 этого кода пути ещё нет, поэтому там всё работает.

issues.title: [macOS 27] App crashes when opening the menu-bar icon due to Qt NSEvent.clickCount assertion
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

AmneziaVPN crashes immediately when its menu-bar icon/menu is opened on macOS 27.

The crash occurs on the main thread inside Qt’s Cocoa system-tray implementation. It appears to be caused by Qt calling `NSEvent.clickCount` when `NSApp.currentEvent` is not a mouse event.

## To reproduce

1. Launch AmneziaVPN.
2. Click the AmneziaVPN icon in the macOS menu bar.
3. The application terminates and macOS generates a crash report.

## Expected behavior

The menu-bar menu should open normally without terminating the application.

## Actual behavior

The application aborts with `EXC_CRASH (SIGABRT)`:

```text
Exception Type: EXC_CRASH (SIGABRT)
Termination Reason: Namespace SIGNAL, Code 6, Abort trap: 6
Application Specific Information:
abort() called

AppKit       -[NSEvent clickCount]
libqcocoa    + 217456
```

The `libqcocoa.dylib + 217456` address resolves to:

```text
QCocoaSystemTrayIcon::emitActivated()
```

## Environment

- AmneziaVPN: 5.0.0, bundle build 5
- Bundled Qt version: 6.10.1
- macOS: 27.0, build 26A5388g
- Mac: MacBook Pro 14-inch 2021 (`MacBookPro18,3`)
- Processor: Apple M1 Pro
- Architecture: ARM64
- SIP: Enabled

## Suspected root cause

Qt 6.10.1 calls `NSApp.currentEvent.clickCount` without first verifying that the current event is a mouse event:

https://github.com/qt/qtbase/blob/v6.10.1/src/plugins/platforms/cocoa/qcocoasystemtrayicon.mm

Qt’s development branch already contains a guard specifically explaining that macOS 27 now drives `NSControl` through gesture recognizers, so `NSApp.currentEvent` may not be a mouse event:

https://github.com/qt/qtbase/blob/dev/src/plugins/platforms/cocoa/qcocoasystemtrayicon.mm

The relevant fix checks `qt_mac_isMouseEvent(NSApp.currentEvent)` before accessing `clickCount`.

Please consider applying or backporting this Qt fix to the macOS build.

## Log files

A complete macOS crash report is attached.

issues.title: XRay/VLESS server config regenerated inconsistently on every settings interaction — Reality silently dropped, keys rotate, flow+security mismatch causes silent connection failure
issues.body:
**Summary**
On a self-hosted AmneziaVPN server, interacting with XRay protocol settings in the client (even without intentionally changing anything) causes the server-side XRay config to be regenerated from scratch rather than edited in place. Across repeated tests on the same server, this produced at least three different, inconsistent outcomes — including one combination that connects but never passes traffic, and one that fails to connect immediately. This makes XRay effectively unusable for any setup with more than one client device, since managing multiple devices requires touching the server config, which is precisely what triggers the regression.

**Environment**
- Server: self-hosted, Ubuntu 24.04, official Amnezia install, XRay running in the `amnezia-xray` Docker container (alongside separate `amnezia-awg` / `amnezia-awg2` containers for AmneziaWG, unaffected by this bug)
- Clients tested: AmneziaVPN 5.0.0.5 on Windows 11, and AmneziaVPN 5.0.0.5 on Android — both linked to the same server, with client sync/admin enabled between the two devices
- Also tested AmneziaVPN 4.8.15.4 on Windows 11 for comparison (see "Related" below)

**What we observed, condensed from a full day of testing**

1. **Config regeneration on every touch.** Every time the XRay protocol settings were opened/saved on either device (Windows or Android) for the same server, `/opt/amnezia/xray/server.json` inside the container was rewritten with a brand-new `privateKey`. This happened even when no field was intentionally changed. This is the same root cause as #1225 (editing an existing XRay connection is not supported — any change effectively recreates it).

2. **`security` field is inconsistent across regenerations.** Checked directly on the server after each client interaction:
   - Sometimes: `"security": "reality"` with a full, valid `realitySettings` block (privateKey, dest, serverNames, shortIds) — Reality correctly configured.
   - Sometimes: `"security": ""` — Reality silently absent, **while the client UI still displayed "Reality" as the active/selected setting for that server**, with no error or warning shown to the user.
   - We captured this transition at least 4 times across the session, purely by re-opening settings / toggling unrelated fields (e.g., `flow`) and saving again — no deliberate attempt to disable Reality was made.

3. **`flow` + `security: none` is a silently broken combination.** When testing with an independent client (v2rayNG on Android, using a hand-built `vless://` link derived directly from the server's actual `server.json`) to rule out client-side bugs:
   - `flow=xtls-rprx-vision` + `security=none` → connection fails immediately ("no internet" — fast failure, not a hang).
   - Same UUID's sibling client entry (no `flow` set) + `security=none` → connects and works normally, full speed.
   
   This suggests the server is willing to accept and serve a `clients[]` entry combining `flow: xtls-rprx-vision` with no `security`/Reality at all, which is a nonsensical combination (XTLS-Vision expects a TLS layer underneath), but the client silently generates such configs without validation.

4. **UI shows "connected but hangs forever" vs "connection fails fast" as different symptoms of different broken states**, which made this hard to diagnose without directly inspecting the server-side JSON — the client gives no indication of which underlying state it is in.

**Example configs captured (keys redacted)**

Working (independent client, `security: none`, no flow):
```json
{
    "inbounds": [{
        "port": 443,
        "protocol": "vless",
        "settings": {
            "clients": [
                { "flow": "xtls-rprx-vision", "id": "<uuid-1>" },
                { "id": "<uuid-2>" }
            ],
            "decryption": "none"
        },
        "streamSettings": { "network": "tcp", "security": "" }
    }],
    "outbounds": [{ "protocol": "freedom" }]
}
```
`<uuid-2>` (no flow) connects and works. `<uuid-1>` (flow set)

issues.title: [iOS 5.0.0.5] CIDR prefix is stripped from imported site-based split-tunneling entries
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

When a site-based split-tunneling JSON file contains an IPv4 CIDR in the `hostname` field, AmneziaVPN 5.0.0.5 removes the prefix length during import.

For example:

```json
{ "hostname": "1.192.0.0/10", "ip": "" }
```

is stored and passed to the iOS Network Extension as:

```text
1.192.0.0
```

As a result, AmneziaWG creates a host route for only the network address instead of routing the intended subnet. A CIDR-based split-tunneling list therefore appears to import successfully but does not work.

This was reproduced on iOS with AmneziaWG 2. The UI mode, `AllowedIPs`, tunnel startup, and handshake are all correct; only the CIDR masks are lost.

**To Reproduce**

1. Disconnect the VPN.
2. Open **Settings → Connection → Site-based split tunneling**.
3. Enable split tunneling.
4. Select **Only the sites listed here will be accessed through the VPN**.
5. Import the attached `amnezia-cidr-import-minimal-repro.json` using **Replace existing list**.
6. Observe that the UI displays `1.192.0.0` and `2.16.0.0`, without `/10` and `/13`.
7. Connect using AmneziaWG 2.
8. Export the application log and inspect `SplitTunnelSites`.

**Actual behavior**

The CIDR prefix lengths are removed:

```text
AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0
SplitTunnelType = 1
SplitTunnelSites = 1.192.0.0, 2.16.0.0, 1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1
```

In a real list containing thousands of CIDRs, the exported log contained zero `/` characters in `SplitTunnelSites`. The Network Extension accepted the resulting routes and the VPN handshake succeeded, but traffic for the intended subnets was not routed through the VPN.

The attached before/after evidence was collected from the same iPhone, app build, AmneziaWG 2 profile, and route mode:

| Import representation | Split-tunnel entries | Entries retaining CIDR | Applied IPv4 routes | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Official Amnezia format (`CIDR` in `hostname`) | 3,241 | 0 | 3,242 | Incorrect: subnet masks lost |
| Workaround (`CIDR` in `ip`) | 2,988 including two DNS hosts | 2,986 | 2,989 | Correct: masks retained and tunnel works |

The successful run logged:

```text
AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0
SplitTunnelType = 1
SplitTunnelSites = 1.0.0.0/9, 1.192.0.0/10, ...
Network settings (start): ... ipv4 inc/exc=2989/1 ...
setNetworkSettings: applying
Tunnel interface is utun5
Received handshake response
handshake confirmed
```

This comparison rules out an iOS route-table limitation and an AmneziaWG CIDR parsing problem for this reproduction. The same 5.0.0.5 tunnel works when the importer does not pass CIDRs through `normalizeHostname()`.

**Expected behavior**

CIDR entries must be preserved exactly during import and passed to the tunnel:

```text
SplitTunnelSites = 1.192.0.0/10, 2.16.0.0/13, ...
```

**Log files**

Attach `AmneziaVPN-CIDR-bug-sanitized.log`. It contains sanitized evidence from both the failing and successful runs. The full `AmneziaVPN 2.log` is intentionally not attached because it contains the VPN server endpoint and internal connection identifiers.

**Screenshots**

Attach `IMG_8192.PNG`. It shows that imported CIDR entries are displayed without their prefix lengths while the correct split-tunneling mode is enabled.

**Smartphone (please complete the following information):**

- Device: iPhone (exact model unknown)
- OS: iOS 26.6 (arm64)
- App version: AmneziaVPN 5.0.0.5, commit `4d28f819`
- Protocol: AmneziaWG 2 (`amnezia-awg2`)

**Additional context / suspected root cause**

The problem appears to be in `IpSplitTunnelingController::normalizeHostname()`:

```cpp
normalized = normalized.split("/", Qt::SkipEmptyParts).first();
```

`importSitesFromJson()` calls this function for every `hostname`, including valid CIDR strings. Therefore `/10`, `/13`, `/24`, etc. are treated like URL paths and removed before validation and storage.

Source:

https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amnezia-client/blob/5.0.0.5/client/core/controllers/ipSplitTunnelingController.cpp#L140-L227

The current official Amnezia JSON

issues.title: Split tunneling: a network entered in the site list loses its prefix length and becomes a /32 host
issues.body:
## Summary

Any IPv4 network typed into the split tunneling site list is stored without its prefix length. `84.252.144.0/20` becomes `84.252.144.0`, which the app then applies as a single `/32` host. The network is silently reduced to one address, so the exclusion does nothing. There is no error and the UI shows the entry as accepted.

The same happens when a site list is imported from JSON.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| App | AmneziaVPN 5.0.0 |
| OS | macOS 26.5.2 (arm64) |
| Mode | Sites: *All sites except the listed ones* |

The defect is in shared code, so it is not specific to macOS.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open split tunneling settings and pick *All sites except the listed ones*.
2. Add `84.252.144.0/20`.
3. Connect, then look at the routing table and at the `allownets` table of the `amn` pf anchor.

## Expected

The list holds `84.252.144.0/20`, and the app installs a route and a firewall entry for the whole `/20`.

## Actual

The list holds `84.252.144.0`. Both halves are installed for a `/32`:

```
84.252.144/32   <gateway>   UGSc   en0
```

```
allownets: 84.252.144.0
```

Everything else in the pipeline is correct — the route and the firewall entry are created, they just cover one address instead of 4096.

## Where it happens

`IpSplitTunnelingController::normalizeHostname` in `client/core/controllers/ipSplitTunnelingController.cpp`:

```cpp
normalized = normalized.split("/", Qt::SkipEmptyParts).first();
```

The line is meant to cut the path off a URL such as `example.com/page`. It also cuts the prefix length off a CIDR.

Nothing downstream catches it. `NetworkUtilities::ipAddressWithSubnetRegExp` treats the `/NN` suffix as optional, so `84.252.144.0` passes validation as a plain address.

`IpSplitTunnelingController::importSitesFromJson` calls the same function, so importing a list does not work around this.

## Suggested fix

Return early when the input already is a valid address or network:

```cpp
QString IpSplitTunnelingController::normalizeHostname(const QString &hostname) const
{
    QString normalized = hostname.trimmed();
    normalized.replace("https://", "");
    normalized.replace("http://", "");
    normalized.replace("ftp://", "");
    if (NetworkUtilities::checkIpSubnetFormat(normalized)) {
        return normalized;
    }
    normalized = normalized.split("/", Qt::SkipEmptyParts).first();
    return normalized;
}
```

Existing lists already saved with a stripped prefix will stay broken, so a note in the release notes may be worth it.

issues.title: [VLESS] [Ubuntu 24.04] systemd-resolved crashes with 'start-limit-hit' when split tunneling is enabled
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
When split tunneling is enabled on Ubuntu 24.04, the `systemd-resolved.service` crashes due to a restart loop, leading to a complete DNS resolution failure (e.g., YouTube and other domains stop resolving). 

The system logs show that `systemd-resolved.service` hits its start limit because the client (or associated scripts) triggers service restarts too rapidly. Manually starting the service afterwards temporarily fixes the issue.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Connect to a VLESS server on Ubuntu 24.04.
2. Enable Split Tunneling mode.
3. Attempt to open a website (e.g., YouTube) and observe that DNS resolution fails.
4. Check service status via `sudo systemctl status systemd-resolved.service`.
5. See the error: `Failed with result 'start-limit-hit'`.
6. Fix temporarily by running: `sudo systemctl enable --now systemd-resolved.service`

**Expected behavior**
Enabling or disabling split tunneling modes should handle DNS configuration smoothly without causing `systemd-resolved.service` to rapidly restart, trigger rate limits, and crash.

**Log files**
`systemd-resolved` service failure state:
```text
systemd-resolved.service: Start request repeated too quickly.
systemd-resolved.service: Failed with result 'start-limit-hit'
```

Reference Routing Table (Split Tunneling **Enabled**):
```text
0.0.0.0/1 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
default via 192.168.0.1 dev enp3s0 proto dhcp src 192.168.0.193 metric 100
8.8.4.4 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
10.33.0.0/24 dev tun2 proto kernel scope link src 10.33.0.2
100.64.0.1 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
128.0.0.0/1 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope Link
```

Reference Routing Table (Split Tunneling **Disabled**):
```text
default via 192.168.0.1 dev enp3s0 proto dhcp src 192.168.0.193 metric 100
1.0.0.0/8 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
2.0.0.0/7 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
4.0.0.0/6 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
8.0.0.0/5 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
8.8.4.4 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
10.33.0.0/24 dev tun2 proto kernel scope link src 10.33.0.2
16.0.0.0/4 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
32.0.0.0/3 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
64.0.0.0/2 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
100.64.0.1 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
128.0.0.0/1 via 10.33.0.2 dev tun2 scope link
```

**Desktop:**
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- Version: 4.8.21.0

**Server:**

**Additional context**
The issue is strictly related to how AmneziaVPN interacts with `systemd-resolved` when modifying the routing table and DNS parameters during the split tunneling state transition. The application triggers too many rapid restart requests for the service, hitting systemd's default protective rate limits.

issues.title: [macOS] wireguard-go is x86_64 only — causes 5-10 min connection delay on Apple Silicon (website build)
issues.body:
## Description

On Apple Silicon Macs (M1/M2/M3/M4), the website build of AmneziaVPN takes 5-10 minutes 
to connect when using AmneziaWG v2 protocol. The App Store build connects in under 10 seconds.

## Root cause

The `wireguard-go` binary shipped in the website build is x86_64 only:

$ file /Applications/AmneziaVPN.app/Contents/MacOS/wireguard-go
/Applications/AmneziaVPN.app/Contents/MacOS/wireguard-go: Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64

On Apple Silicon it runs under Rosetta 2, which causes a very long startup time. 
The App Store build for iOS ships a native binary (arm64), which is why it works fine. Simple install it in your Mac

## Steps to reproduce

1. Download AmneziaVPN from the official website (not App Store)
2. Install on Apple Silicon Mac (tested on M4 Pro)
3. Add AmneziaWG v2 connection
4. Press Connect — takes 5-10 minutes

From the logs, the delay is entirely between daemon receiving the connect command 
and wireguard-go completing startup:

[20:54:13] Parse command: status   ← connect initiated
[21:01:10] Parse command: connected ← 7 minutes later

## Environment

- macOS Tahoe 26.3.1
- AmneziaVPN 4.8.15.4 (website build)
- Hardware: MacBook Pro M4 Pro
- Protocol: AmneziaWG v2

## Fix

Ship `wireguard-go` as a native binary (arm64) in the website build, 
same as the App Store build.


https://apps.apple.com/us/app/amneziavpn/id1600529900

issues.title: DNS nameserver doesn't revert to default after VPN disconnection
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Upon disconnecting from the VPN, DNS nameserver doesn't revert to default value

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Before connecting to the VPN, run the command: cat /etc/resolv.conf. You should see the following line in the file: nameserver 192.168.0.1 (this DNS is provided by my DHCP server).
2. Connect to the VPN using the XRay protocol in Amnezia.
3. Check the /etc/resolv.conf file again, and you will see that nameserver 192.168.0.1 has been replaced by 1.1.1.1.
4. Disconnect from the VPN and check /etc/resolv.conf again. The nameserver remains set to 1.1.1.1 instead of reverting to the DHCP-provided value, 192.168.0.1.

**Expected behavior**
Upon disconnecting from the VPN, the DNS should revert to the DHCP-assigned value (192.168.0.1) rather than remaining at 1.1.1.1.

issues.title: fix: handle large Linux route dumps
issues.body:
## Summary
- read multipart Linux route dumps without overflowing the original 8 KiB buffer
- select only the IPv4 default route from matching netlink responses
- skip empty WireGuard endpoint addresses and fail activation when endpoint exclusion cannot be installed
- add a Linux regression test for default-gateway discovery

## Root cause
On systems with a larger routing table, such as Ubuntu 24.04 with container or bridge routes, the `RTM_GETROUTE` dump exceeded the fixed 8192-byte buffer. The receive loop then failed before parsing the existing default route. `LinuxRouteMonitor` consequently skipped the VPN endpoint exclusion route, after which the `/1` full-tunnel routes sent the WireGuard transport back into `amn0`.

An empty IPv6 endpoint was also passed to `IPAddress`, producing the unrelated `/999999` warning.

## Validation
- reproduced with AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 / `amnezia-awg2` on Ubuntu 24.04
- regression test passed on Ubuntu 24.04 with 300 additional routes, making the dump larger than the original 8 KiB buffer
- `git diff --check` passes
- verified that the broad routing implementation remains unchanged; this is a focused hotfix

issues.title: Linux 5.0.1.5: exclusion routes never installed — netlink route dump overflows the   fixed 8 KiB buffer
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

  On Linux, client 5.0.1.5 fails to read the routing table and never installs
  exclusion routes for the VPN endpoint. With `0.0.0.0/1` and `128.0.0.0/1`
  pointing at the tunnel, WireGuard packets addressed to the server are routed
  back into the tunnel itself, creating a routing loop. Packets grow with each
  iteration until the socket rejects them with `sendmmsg: message too long`.

  Client 4.8.21 on the very same machine installs the routes correctly and works.
  The issue is protocol-independent — reproduced with both AmneziaWG 2.0 and 3.1
  servers.

  **To Reproduce**

  Steps to reproduce the behavior:
  1. Install 5.0.1.5 on Ubuntu 24.04 with a normal DHCP default route
  2. Connect to any AmneziaWG server
  3. Run `ip route get <server-ip>` — it points at the tunnel (`dev amn0`) instead
     of the physical gateway
  4. See `sendmmsg: message too long` in the daemon log; no traffic passes

  **Expected behavior**

  The daemon should add an exclusion route for the server endpoint through the
  physical default gateway, as 4.8.21 does:
  ```
  <server-ip> via 192.168.31.1 dev wlp0s20f3
  ```

  **Log files**

  Same 15-second window, two client versions on one machine:

  | Log line | 5.0.1.5 | 4.8.21 |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Error in received packet: Numerical argument out of domain` | 10 | 0 |
  | `No default gateway available, skipping exclusion route` | 10 | 0 |
  | exclusion routes actually installed | none | all |

5.0.1.5:
  ```
  LinuxRouteMonitor : Adding exclusion route for <server-ip>/32
  Error in received packet: No such file or directory
  LinuxRouteMonitor : No default gateway available, skipping exclusion route
  ...
  WireguardGo : ERROR: (amn0) peer(XXXX…) - Failed to send data packets:
                write udp 0.0.0.0:54793: sendmmsg: message too long
  ```
  
  4.8.21, same step:
  ```
  LinuxRouteMonitor : Adding exclusion route for <server-ip>/32
  ```
  (no warning, route present in `ip route`)
  
  Other errors present in both versions, possibly related:
  ``` 
  Error: argument "amnvpnrt" is wrong: table id value is invalid
  mkdir: cannot create directory '/sys/fs/cgroup/net_cls/amnvpnexclusions/'
  LinuxRouteMonitor : Adding exclusion route for /999999 → Invalid destination prefix
  net_cls cgroup v1 not available, traffic splitting disabled
  ```
  
  **Screenshots**
  
  N/A — the client reports "Connected".

  **Desktop (please complete the following information):**
   - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (kernel 6.17), KDE Plasma / X11
   - Version: 5.0.1.5 (regression — 4.8.21 works)

  **Smartphone (please complete the following information):**
   - Not affected — mobile clients handle routing through the OS VPN API

  **Server (please complete the following information):**
   - OS: Ubuntu 24.04, Docker

**Additional context**
  
  Workaround — add the exclusion route manually before connecting:
  ```
  sudo ip route add <server-ip> via <lan-gateway> dev <iface>
  ```
  The loop disappears and `sendmmsg: message too long` stops.
  
  Possibly related: #1498, #1357, #2048 — all report "connected but no internet"
  on Linux with the same `amnvpnrt` / `Invalid destination prefix` log noise.

issues.title: fix(linux): read the default gateway from /proc/net/route
issues.body:
## Summary

Replace the netlink `RTM_GETROUTE` dump parsing in
`NetworkUtilities::getGatewayAndIface()` (Linux) with a read of the main IPv4
table from `/proc/net/route`.

## Root cause

`getGatewayAndIface()` reads the routing table into a fixed 8 KiB buffer. On any
host with more than ~100 routes the dump does not fit, the gateway comes back
empty, and `LinuxRouteMonitor` skips **every** exclusion route:

```
Adding exclusion route for 37.130.192.0/22
No default gateway available, skipping exclusion route
```

The function is also called once per exclusion route (RTN_THROW branch in
`LinuxRouteMonitor::addExclusionRoute`). Each call re-dumps a table that has
just grown by one route, so even a larger buffer only moves the failure point:
with a 3 319-entry split-tunnelling list the dump grows past 128 KiB long before
the list ends.

`/proc/net/route` exposes the same main table (`rtm_table == RT_TABLE_MAIN`),
has no size limit and costs one small read per lookup.

## Changes

- `client/core/utils/networkUtilities.cpp`: pick the default route
  (`Destination == 00000000`) with the lowest metric, decode the gateway and
  interface name from `/proc/net/route`.
- Drop the now unused netlink/socket includes.

## Validation

- Arch Linux host with 113 routes (the state in which the old code returned an
  empty gateway): patched function returns `192.168.0.1` / `wlp0s20f3`.
- Real AmneziaWG session with a 3 319-entry exclusion list:
  - before: 3 319 `No default gateway available`, none installed;
  - after: all routes installed; `ip route get 92.255.99.232` goes through the
    physical gateway instead of `amn0`, and the site that was unreachable over
    the foreign exit loads.
- `git diff --check` clean, `git clang-format` no changes.
- Not tested: Windows/macOS (untouched), IPv6-only uplinks (the function was
  IPv4-only before as well).

## Test plan

No unit test: the function depends on the host routing table. Manual check:
connect AmneziaWG with a large exclusion list, confirm the service log has no
`No default gateway available` and that `ip route get <excluded ip>` uses the
uplink interface.

Refs: #3090, #3170, #3231.

issues.title: fix: Linux DNS resolution with the kill switch enabled + OpenVPN container NAT
issues.body:
## Summary

Three related Linux fixes, discovered while investigating broken name
resolution on ALT Linux (ALT bug #52679).

### 1. Fall back to resolvconf when /etc/resolv.conf is not managed by systemd-resolved

The per-link DNS configuration set through the resolved D-Bus API is only
consumed by applications that use the systemd-resolved stub resolver. On
distributions where /etc/resolv.conf is managed by another tool
(resolvconf/NetworkManager), applications keep querying the pre-existing
resolvers, which are either unreachable from the tunnel or rejected by the
kill switch. When resolv.conf does not point to systemd-resolved, the tunnel
resolvers are now pushed into the system resolver via resolvconf (the same
mechanism the bundled OpenVPN update-resolv-conf script uses), and the entry
is removed on disconnect.

### 2. Keep the current system DNS servers reachable with the kill switch enabled

The `320.allowDNS` anchor only accepted DNS traffic to the tunnel DNS servers
leaving via one of the tunnel interfaces. A system configured with other
resolvers (e.g. a local router) could not resolve anything at all once the
kill switch was enabled — and it is enabled by default, so DNS appeared
completely broken. The nameservers currently present in /etc/resolv.conf are
read when the kill switch is enabled and added to the allow list with rules
not restricted to the tunnel interfaces.

### 3. Mount /lib/modules into the OpenVPN container

The container start script configures NAT with iptables, which fails inside
the container when it cannot load the legacy netfilter modules from
/lib/modules (`iptables who? (do you need to insmod?)`). Without NAT the
tunnel carries no traffic at all. Mount the host modules read-only so the
rules are applied; on hosts without the modules the mount is harmless.

## Testing

ALT Linux Sisyphus, client 5.1.0.6: AmneziaWG and OpenVPN with the kill
switch enabled now resolve via both getaddrinfo and direct /etc/resolv.conf
readers; OpenVPN tunnels work after container reinstallation.
